title: Artificial Intelligence, Productivity, and the Workforce: Evidence from Corporate Executives
source_location: Figure 1, Total employment row, printed page 7 / PDF page 8. Values checked against original figure.
survey: 734 US senior financial executives, primarily CFOs, surveyed near year-end 2025. CFO Survey (Duke, Richmond Fed, Atlanta Fed), supplemented by FEI, NASDAQ and Duke alumni respondents.
units: Percent change in own-firm total employment attributed to AI use: reported 2025 and anticipated 2026. Size-group averages, not economy-wide employment changes.
size_groups: Small: fewer than 500 employees; large: 500 or more employees.
construction: Authors convert categorical responses to numerical averages using category midpoints; open upper/lower categories use 5 percentage points beyond the boundary. No change is zero; not sure is missing. Plotted values are the published rounded means, not independently computed microdata estimates.
interpretation: Self-reported and expected AI effects, not an independently identified causal estimate or observed 2026 administrative job loss.
refresh_policy: Update the four values only from a verified new version of Figure 1; keep source version and metadata synchronized.
